newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower in quiet trade.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Monday, as the U.S. dollar surged to new 31-month highs against the mark and new 46 month highs against yen, but trade was dampened by the US Martin Luther King holiday which closed government offices and banks.
"The only feature of the day was funds rolling short positions from February to April in gold, crushing the spread," FIMAT trader John Tyree said.
COMEX February gold ended down $1.80 an ounce at $354.60, after seeing a session low at $353.40, just above the contract low at $352.60 seen last week.
Estimated total COMEX gold futures volume was 25,000 lots.
The February/April spread narrowed to $1.60 an ounce, from $1.80 Friday, a 12-month low for the contango.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $353.30/80, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $353.10 and the New York close Friday at $355.30/80.
Gold appeared to be consolidating again just above $350 an ounce, after sliding to three year lows in the first week of 1997, analysts said.
"In gold a historical perspective is necessary because many buyers are still attempting to pick bottoms because they think gold is cheap," Commodities Research Bureau analyst Terry Roggensack said.
"But back in 1993 the monthly charts had gold down to $325, a full $25 below the current market," he said.

"Volume statistics on the current market are interesting because January has maintained the highest average daily volume in almost a year and we would not be comfortable picking the bottom off increased volume alone."

The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data for the week ended January 14, released late Friday, showed fund net short open interest in gold up 11,044 lots to 52,969 lots in the past two week, but most of the rise occurred in the first week of January.
And gold open interest fell late last week, suggesting some fund shortcovering had begun occurring again, analysts noted.
The spot gold/silver ratio managed a gain for the first time in a week also, ending at 74.85 Monday, from 74.48 Friday which was a four month low.
COMEX March silver closed down 4.00 cents at $4.732, after seeing a session low at $4.710.
The CFTC data showed funds had re-established a small net short position in silver, as of January 14, reversing from a small net long position on December 31.
But "every second year, in February or March, the silver market tends to bottom and usually attempts a rally," Smith Barney technical analyst Rick Lorusso said.
"This periodic cycle is due again in 1997 and the last two cycles in 1993 and 1995 produced rallies of $1.905 and $1.820 an ounce respectively," he said.
"It is less effective in bear markets, but with prices above the last two cycle lows, expectations for a sizable recovery appear justified."
Gold was stronger than platinum also Monday, with the April COMEX gold/NYMEX platinum spread falling to $5.00 an ounce from $7.00 Friday and a two month high at $9.00 last week.
NYMEX April platinum closed down $3.80 an ounce at new life-of-contract lows at $361.20.
NYMEX March palladium ended down $1.00 at $124.00.
